mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates economic expansion, which may boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next month.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is positive but S&P returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate increased construction activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next quarter.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low and unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it may indicate economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investors become risk-averse.
failure_condition: If the condition is met but S&P returns are positive more than 30% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) may signal reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are affected.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows but S&P returns remain positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) may lead to inflation concerns, prompting tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: If CPI increases but S&P returns are positive more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, which may boost corporate revenues and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next quarter.
failure_condition: If retail sales grow but S&P returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases but is accompanied by rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), it may lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.
